{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|Centuries of pooled experience by Guildmembers led to the SEPI principle, which is still the best distillation of what goes into a successful hunt. It's a simple but endlessly adaptable framework. Under SEPI, every hunter consists of four consecutive stages: Selection, Evaluation, Preparation, and Implementation,|Ro-San Borokki, Bounty Hunters' Guild Handbook|<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>}}
The '''SEPI principle''' was a stock formula that was applied by [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] in pursuit of their quarry and was regarded among professional [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]] as the unwritten law of the proper approach to claiming a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]].<ref name="GG10">''[[Galaxy Guide 10: Bounty Hunters]]''</ref> The SEPI framework was developed by members of the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]], who drew from centuries of bounty hunting experience when formulating the principle, and the SEPI approach was outlined with the [[Bounty Hunters Guild Handbook]], in a chapter written by the veteran hunter [[Ro-San Borokki]].<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" /> The principle stressed that there were four stages to a successful hunt: selection, evaluation, preparation and implementation, directing bounty hunters to only pursue suitable targets, seek sufficient information to perform a proper evaluation of their target's situation, apply proper planning as to the method of capture of the target, then apply sufficient resources when ultimately attempting to take down the target.<ref name="GG10" />
